workingIdentity: Dark History: short, true, documented stories
format: Faceless documentary Shorts: real archival images with slow motion, a calm public-domain voice, burned-in captions
corePromise: A real shipwreck, disappearance or disaster told in under a minute, only from what the sources state, with every image credited.
audience: Global English-speaking viewers who like true history, unsolved mysteries and documentary storytelling.

primaryFormat.shortsRole: Core channel identity and primary publishing surface.

storyCriteria: The event is real, at least 50 years old, and involves no living person.
Every beat has relevant, license-checked real images; a beat without one is dropped, never filled.
Every claim maps to a source sentence (verbatim evidence); numbers, names and quotations are in the source.
The Wikipedia text credit and the author, license and URL of every image go into the description unchanged.
The Short fits 35-58 seconds and normally 70-100 spoken words.
avoid: Invented detail, emotion, motive, dialogue or certainty.
AI-generated images of real events, or stand-in images.
Living people, recent tragedies, graphic gore as the main appeal.
Near-duplicate stories or a template that makes every Short look the same.

publishingCadence.initialPolicy: Up to 3 Shorts per day (21 per week) while the story pool holds 14 days of stories; fewer when it runs low.
publishingCadence.schedulingPolicy: Autonomous mode assigns safe Shorts publish slots.
publishingCadence.qualityPolicy: Cadence is subordinate to quality: a gate that fails rejects the Short, no gate is relaxed to keep the pace, and a low story pool lowers the cadence.

brandTagline: True stories, told from the record.
channelDescription: Short, true, documented stories of shipwrecks, disappearances and disasters, told from the historical record with real archival images. Sources and image credits are in every description.
